packages.name: gibson.agentidentity.v1
packages.comment:
Package gibson.agentidentity.v1 — AgentIdentityService: customer-callable
machine-identity provisioning surface and the developer enrollment dev-loop
(`gibson component register` / `gibson agent`). Re-homed out of
gibson.tenant.v1 into its own wire package so it can stay in the OSS SDK
while the nine tenant-administration services move to the gibson platform
protos under the unchanged gibson.tenant.v1 package — keeping both in one
package would link two generated Go homes for gibson.tenant.v1 into the
daemon (proto: duplicate registration). See ADR-0058 (amended 2026-06-22).

services.name: AgentIdentityService
services.comment:
AgentIdentityService provisions and manages machine identities for agents,
tools, and plugins.

methods.name: CreateAgentIdentity
methods.comment:
CreateAgentIdentity provisions a new machine identity for an agent, tool,
or plugin. Returns a one-time capability-grant bootstrap_token that cannot
be recovered after this call (ADR-0045 — the unified enrollment credential
for every kind).

methods.name: ListAgentIdentities
methods.comment:
ListAgentIdentities returns all agent/tool/plugin identities provisioned in
the caller's tenant, with optional kind filtering and pagination.

methods.name: RevokeAgentIdentity
methods.comment:
RevokeAgentIdentity permanently revokes a machine identity. Existing JWTs
stop validating within the IdP token TTL (<=60 seconds). Idempotent on
already-revoked principals (returns NotFound).

messages.comment: AgentIdentity is a single entry in the list response.

fields.comment:

fields.comment:
bootstrap_token is a one-time, daemon-signed Capability-Grant bootstrap
credential the component presents to the CG register endpoint to complete
its FIRST host registration (it carries no Capability Grant yet). Under the
unified-identity model (ADR-0045) this is the SOLE credential `gibson
component register` uses for every kind; the enroll_command pipes it via
`--token -`. Store it immediately; it will not be shown again.

packages.name: gibson.budget_status.v1
packages.comment:
Package gibson.budget_status.v1 — public, customer-visible wire shapes
for LLM budget status signals.

BudgetScope and BudgetExceeded are the wire-level types that:
 - the daemon attaches to a codes.ResourceExhausted gRPC status as
 a status-detail when an ExecuteLLM call is denied for budget
 reasons (see internal/daemon/api/server_provider_exec.go); and
 - the SDK exposes back to customer agent code through
 llm.BudgetExceededError and llm.IsBudgetExceeded (see
 llm/errors.go).

Both surfaces share these types — the customer-facing READ side lives
in the public OSS SDK (this package); the tenant-admin WRITE-side
service that mutates budgets (gibson.budget.v1.BudgetService) lives
in the internal platform-sdk. Customer agent code branching on
budget denial parses BudgetExceeded directly out of the gRPC status
detail without needing the admin service descriptor.

This mirrors the sdk#103 pattern that did the same separation for
gibson.capability.v1.CapabilityGrantInfo (READ side in OSS) vs
gibson.admin.v1.GrantsAdminService (WRITE side in platform-sdk).

Spec: llm-user-attribution-governance (Requirement 3, READ-side
 wire contract); two-surface platform contract
 (ADR-0025 / ADR-0030, sdk#106).

messages.name: BudgetExceeded
messages.comment:
BudgetExceeded is the status-detail payload returned inside the
codes.ResourceExhausted gRPC status when an LLM call is denied for
budget reasons. Consumers unmarshal via SDK helper IsBudgetExceeded.

Field numbers + tag names are wire-identical to the original
definition in gibson.budget.v1.BudgetExceeded; see sdk#106 for the
relocation rationale. Customer code branching on budget denial
continues to receive the same on-wire bytes.

fields.name: dimension
fields.comment: dimension is one of "tokens" or "spend".

fields.name: subject_id
fields.comment: subject_id is the limiting subject (user or team ID; empty for tenant).

enums.name: BudgetScope
enums.comment:
BudgetScope identifies the subject class a budget applies to. Tenant is
the rollup ceiling; user and team are subdivisions within a tenant.

Field numbers + enum-value names are wire-identical to the original
definition in gibson.budget.v1; see sdk#106 for the relocation rationale.

packages.name: gibson.capability.v1
packages.comment:
Package gibson.capability.v1 — public, customer-visible wire shape
for capability grants (CG-JWTs).

CapabilityGrantInfo describes ONE active capability grant minted for
an agent / tool / plugin install. It is the read-side projection
returned by:
 - gibson.identity.v1.IdentityService.WhoAmI
 (a principal listing its own active grants)
 - gibson.admin.v1.GrantsAdminService.ListActiveGrants
 (a tenant_admin inspecting all grants in the tenant)

Both surfaces share this type — the READ side lives in the public OSS
SDK (this package); the WRITE/inspector SERVICE that mutates grants
lives in the internal platform-sdk. Customer code that embeds the
agent runtime parses CapabilityGrantInfo to render "what can I do
right now" UI without needing the admin service descriptor.

Spec: two-surface platform contract (ADR-0001, forthcoming);
 component-bootstrap-e2e Requirement 10 (read side);
 secrets-tenant-lifecycle Requirement 8.1 (write side, moved
 to platform-sdk under slice #108).

messages.name: CapabilityGrantInfo
messages.comment:
CapabilityGrantInfo is the wire-shape for one active capability
grant. It is derived from the daemon's grant store and is suitable
for both the dashboard's grants table and the agent-side "what can
I do right now" UI.

fields.name: jti
fields.comment:
jti is the JWT ID claim of the CG-JWT — the canonical identifier
the dashboard uses for filtering and per-row drill-down.

fields.name: recipient_install_id
fields.comment: recipient_install_id is the install ID this grant was minted for.

fields.name: recipient_class
fields.comment: recipient_class is the class of the install (AGENT / TOOL / PLUGIN).

fields.name: recipient_name
fields.comment: recipient_name is the display name (component name) of the install.

fields.name: allowed_rpcs
fields.comment:
allowed_rpcs is the set of method strings the grant authorizes
(e.g. ["GetCredential", "RecordFinding"]).

fields.name: mission_id
fields.comment:
mission_id is the mission this grant scopes the recipient to.
Empty for non-mission-scoped grants.

fields.name: task_id
fields.comment:
task_id is the task within the mission. Empty when mission_id is
empty or the grant is mission-wide.

fields.name: issued_at_unix
fields.comment: issued_at_unix is the iat claim, Unix seconds.

fields.name: expires_at_unix
fields.comment: expires_at_unix is the exp claim, Unix seconds.

fields.name: near_expiry
fields.comment:
near_expiry is true when the grant expires within 5 minutes from
now. The dashboard renders these rows with a warning highlight.

fields.name: isolation
fields.comment:
isolation is where this grant's untrusted-execution boundary lives
(ADR-0010). UNSPECIFIED is treated as HOSTED_SANDBOX by the daemon's
dispatch-policy gate. Consumed together with the deployment shape:
setec-only permits only HOSTED_SANDBOX (fail-closed otherwise).

enums.name: IsolationMode
enums.comment:
IsolationMode is where the untrusted-execution isolation boundary lives for
a capability grant (ADR-0010). It is consumed by the daemon's dispatch-policy
gate together with the deployment shape (GIBSON_UNTRUSTED_EXEC): under the
hosted SaaS shape (setec-only) only ISOLATION_MODE_HOSTED_SANDBOX is
permitted; any other value is rejected fail-closed. Under a customer-operated
shape (customer-isolation) the customer modes are permitted, and
ISOLATION_MODE_ON_PREM_SANDBOX_ENDPOINT resolves the configured (customer-
pointed) setec SandboxService endpoint.

The enum lives here (public OSS) because callers parsing a
CapabilityGrantInfo need to render the isolation posture without pulling the
admin/mint service descriptor — same rationale as RecipientClass.

values.name: ISOLATION_MODE_UNSPECIFIED
values.comment:
ISOLATION_MODE_UNSPECIFIED is treated as ISOLATION_MODE_HOSTED_SANDBOX by
the gate (back-compat for grants minted before this field shipped), which
is the fail-closed-safe default in the hosted shape.

values.name: ISOLATION_MODE_HOSTED_SANDBOX
values.comment:
ISOLATION_MODE_HOSTED_SANDBOX: untrusted execution runs in the platform-
operated setec sandbox fleet. The only mode permitted under setec-only.

values.name: ISOLATION_MODE_CUSTOMER_CLUSTER_ATTESTED
values.comment:
ISOLATION_MODE_CUSTOMER_CLUSTER_ATTESTED: untrusted execution runs in a
customer-operated cluster whose isolation the daemon verifies by
attestation. Attestation mechanics are a separate follow-up.

values.name: ISOLATION_MODE_CUSTOMER_SELF_SANDBOX
values.comment:
ISOLATION_MODE_CUSTOMER_SELF_SANDBOX: the customer owns and operates the
isolation boundary entirely. Attestation mechanics are a separate
follow-up.

values.name: ISOLATION_MODE_ON_PREM_SANDBOX_ENDPOINT
values.comment:
ISOLATION_MODE_ON_PREM_SANDBOX_ENDPOINT: untrusted execution dispatches to
a customer-pointed setec SandboxService endpoint configured on the daemon.

enums.name: RecipientClass
enums.comment:
RecipientClass is the class of caller a capability grant is issued
to. The runtime enum lives here (public OSS) because callers parsing
a CapabilityGrantInfo need to discriminate without pulling the admin
service descriptor.

values.name: RECIPIENT_CLASS_AGENT
values.comment:
RECIPIENT_CLASS_AGENT: the grant authorizes an agent install to
invoke a per-mission RPC set.

values.name: RECIPIENT_CLASS_TOOL
values.comment: RECIPIENT_CLASS_TOOL: the grant authorizes a tool install.

values.name: RECIPIENT_CLASS_PLUGIN
values.comment: RECIPIENT_CLASS_PLUGIN: the grant authorizes a plugin install.

services.name: ComponentService
services.comment:
ComponentService is the central gRPC service that all Gibson components
(agents, tools, and plugins) connect to. Components register themselves,
receive work via long-polling, submit results, and access harness operations
(LLM completion, tool calls, plugin queries, findings, memory) through
the proxy RPCs defined here.

methods.name: CallTool
methods.comment: CallTool proxies a tool execution request through the agent harness.

methods.name: CallToolStream
methods.comment:
CallToolStream proxies a tool execution with server-side streaming of
progress, partial results, warnings, and the final output.

methods.name: CancelMission
methods.comment: CancelMission requests cancellation of a running mission.

methods.name: Complete
methods.comment: Complete proxies an LLM completion request through the agent harness.

methods.name: CompleteStream
methods.comment: CompleteStream proxies a streaming LLM completion request through the agent harness.

methods.name: CompleteStructured
methods.comment:
CompleteStructured proxies an LLM completion requesting JSON output
conforming to the supplied schema.

methods.name: CompleteWithTools
methods.comment:
CompleteWithTools proxies an LLM completion with tool definitions for
function-calling support. Returns the response including any tool calls.

methods.name: CreateMission
methods.comment: CreateMission creates a new sub-mission.

methods.name: DelegateToAgent
methods.comment: DelegateToAgent dispatches a sub-task to another agent and returns its result.

methods.name: DisablePlugin
methods.comment: DisablePlugin deactivates a plugin for the calling tenant.

methods.name: EnablePlugin
methods.comment:
EnablePlugin activates a plugin for the calling tenant, optionally
supplying an initial configuration JSON blob.

methods.name: FindSimilarAttacks
methods.comment: FindSimilarAttacks returns attack patterns semantically similar to the given content.

methods.name: FindSimilarFindings
methods.comment: FindSimilarFindings returns findings semantically similar to the given finding.

methods.name: GetAttackChains
methods.comment: GetAttackChains returns multi-hop attack paths from a starting technique.

methods.name: GetCredential
methods.comment: GetCredential retrieves a tenant-scoped credential by name.

methods.name: GetFindings
methods.comment: GetFindings queries previously submitted findings with optional filters.

methods.name: GetMissionResults
methods.comment: GetMissionResults returns the final results of a completed mission.

methods.name: GetMissionRunHistory
methods.comment: GetMissionRunHistory returns summaries of previous mission runs.

methods.name: GetMissionStatus
methods.comment: GetMissionStatus returns the current status of a mission.

methods.name: GetPluginConfig
methods.comment: GetPluginConfig retrieves the current configuration and schema for a plugin.

methods.name: GetRelatedFindings
methods.comment: GetRelatedFindings returns findings related to the given finding via graph edges.

methods.name: GetRunFindings
methods.comment: GetRunFindings queries findings scoped to a specific mission run or across all runs.

methods.name: GetTaxonomySchema
methods.comment: GetTaxonomySchema returns the current taxonomy definition.

methods.name: Heartbeat
methods.comment:
Heartbeat sends a periodic health pulse. The response indicates whether
the component is still considered registered and may carry config updates.

methods.name: ListAgents
methods.comment: ListAgents returns descriptors for all agents visible to the caller's tenant.

methods.name: ListAvailablePlugins
methods.comment:
ListAvailablePlugins returns all plugins registered in the system along
with their catalog metadata, health status, and configuration schema.

methods.name: ListMissions
methods.comment: ListMissions returns missions matching the given filter.

methods.name: ListTenantPlugins
methods.comment: ListTenantPlugins returns the plugin access records for the calling tenant.

methods.name: ListTools
methods.comment: ListTools returns descriptors for all tools visible to the caller's tenant.

methods.name: PollWork
methods.comment:
PollWork long-polls for work items assigned to this component instance.
Returns when a work item is available or the server-side timeout expires.

methods.name: QueryNodes
methods.comment: QueryNodes searches the knowledge graph using hybrid vector + graph scoring.

methods.name: QueryPlugin
methods.comment: QueryPlugin proxies a plugin query request through the agent harness.

methods.name: QueueToolWork
methods.comment:
QueueToolWork submits a batch of tool invocations for parallel execution

methods.name: RegisterComponent
methods.comment:
RegisterComponent announces a component to Gibson and receives connection

methods.name: ReportStepHints
methods.comment: ReportStepHints reports planning step hints from an agent back to the orchestrator.

methods.name: RunMission
methods.comment: RunMission queues a mission for execution.

methods.name: SubmitFinding
methods.comment: SubmitFinding submits a security finding through the agent harness.

methods.name: SubmitResult
methods.comment: SubmitResult returns the execution result for a previously polled work item.

methods.name: TestPluginConnection

TestPluginConnection validates connectivity and credentials for a plugin
without persisting any state changes.

methods.name: ToolResults
methods.comment:
ToolResults streams results for a previously queued tool batch as each
invocation completes.

methods.name: UpdatePluginConfig
methods.comment: UpdatePluginConfig replaces the configuration for an already-enabled plugin.

methods.name: WaitMission
methods.comment: WaitMission blocks until a mission completes or the timeout expires.

messages.name: ComponentDescriptor
messages.comment:
ComponentDescriptor is the unified persisted description of a component
registered in the Gibson ComponentRegistry, regardless of how it is
dispatched. Consumers (orchestrator, dashboard, CLI, authz) look up a
descriptor by name and switch on dispatch_mode to choose the routing.

Legacy fields (name, version, kind, tags, metadata) describe every
component. Sandboxed-dispatch fields (image, command, env, resources,
default_timeout_seconds, input_schema_json, output_proto_type,
default_parse_quality) are populated by the daemon's catalog refresher
for sandboxed tools. Plugin/agent entries leave those fields zero.

fields.name: name
fields.comment: Common metadata — populated for every dispatch_mode.

fields.name: image
fields.comment:
Sandboxed-dispatch fields (DISPATCH_MODE_SANDBOXED only).
image is an OCI reference pinned by digest for reproducibility.

fields.name: command
fields.comment: command is the argv the runner executes inside the microVM.

fields.name: env
fields.comment:
env is static environment variables prepended to every Launch call.
The daemon adds GIBSON_TOOL_INPUT_B64 and tracing headers on top.

fields.name: resources
fields.comment: resources is the vCPU + memory budget per sandbox.

fields.name: default_timeout_seconds
fields.comment: default_timeout_seconds bounds the synchronous tool call.

fields.name: input_schema_json
fields.comment:
input_schema_json is the JSON Schema document describing the tool's
typed arguments (fed to the orchestrator LLM for tool_use selection).

fields.name: output_proto_type
fields.comment:
output_proto_type is the fully-qualified proto message name the tool's
response conforms to, e.g. "gibson.tool.nmap.v1.ExecuteResponse".

fields.name: default_parse_quality
fields.comment:
default_parse_quality advertises how richly the runner's parser will
populate the response's field-100 DiscoveryResult for this tool.

fields.name: content_trust
fields.comment:
content_trust classifies the trust level of input data this component
processes at call-time. Consumed by the daemon's dispatch policy gate
together with `dispatch_mode` (see `ContentTrust` doc above).

The default zero (CONTENT_TRUST_UNSPECIFIED) is treated as TRUSTED at
gate-evaluation time for backward compatibility with descriptors
registered before this field existed.

NOTE: field 100 is reserved platform-wide for `gibson.graphrag.DiscoveryResult`
on tool response messages (see `enterprise/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`); do not
assign new fields >= 100 on any component message without coordination.

enums.name: ContentTrust
enums.comment:
ContentTrust classifies the trust level of input data a component will
process at call-time. The daemon's dispatch policy gate consults this
classification together with `dispatch_mode` to decide whether a call may
proceed: an UNTRUSTED component MUST be dispatched via DISPATCH_MODE_SANDBOXED
(microVM) — direct PLUGIN/AGENT execution against UNTRUSTED data is denied
unless a platform-operator override is active.

The default zero value (CONTENT_TRUST_UNSPECIFIED) is treated as TRUSTED by
the gate for backward compatibility with descriptors registered before this
field existed; operators can flip the daemon's `strictDefaultUntrusted=true`
flag to invert that default during a phased rollout.

values.name: CONTENT_TRUST_TRUSTED
values.comment:
CONTENT_TRUST_TRUSTED: input data is sourced from trusted, in-cluster
origins (operator-installed plugins, internal services, vetted manifests)
and may safely run in PLUGIN/AGENT processes.

values.name: CONTENT_TRUST_UNTRUSTED
values.comment:
CONTENT_TRUST_UNTRUSTED: input data is sourced from external networks,
user-supplied targets, or third-party feeds (DNS responses, scanned hosts,
template downloads, etc.). MUST be dispatched via SANDBOXED execution.

enums.name: DispatchMode
enums.comment:
DispatchMode identifies how the Gibson daemon should dispatch calls to a
component registered in the ComponentRegistry. The enum lets one registry
serve tools (sandboxed microVM dispatch), plugins (long-running stateful
gRPC), and agents (long-running gRPC) uniformly — consumers look up by
name and switch on dispatch_mode to choose the route.

values.name: DISPATCH_MODE_SANDBOXED
values.comment:
DISPATCH_MODE_SANDBOXED: the component is a stateless tool executed in
an ephemeral Setec microVM. The registry entry carries image/env/
resources used to Launch the sandbox per call.

values.name: DISPATCH_MODE_PLUGIN
values.comment:
DISPATCH_MODE_PLUGIN: the component is a long-running plugin process
that heartbeats to the registry and serves gRPC.

values.name: DISPATCH_MODE_AGENT
values.comment:
DISPATCH_MODE_AGENT: the component is a long-running agent process that
heartbeats to the registry and serves gRPC.

enums.name: ParseQuality
enums.comment:
ParseQuality tags how richly a sandboxed-tool response populates its
field-100 DiscoveryResult. The taxonomy persistence layer uses this to
filter queries by data quality.

values.name: PARSE_QUALITY_STRUCTURED
values.comment:
PARSE_QUALITY_STRUCTURED: response includes fully populated taxonomy
nodes (Host, Port, Service, Finding,...).

values.name: PARSE_QUALITY_PARTIAL
values.comment:
PARSE_QUALITY_PARTIAL: response includes some taxonomy nodes plus raw
output preserved in Evidence nodes.

values.name: PARSE_QUALITY_RAW
values.comment:
PARSE_QUALITY_RAW: response preserves stdout as an Evidence node only;
no taxonomy-specific nodes were extracted.

values.name: PARSE_QUALITY_FAILED
values.comment:
PARSE_QUALITY_FAILED: a parser errored; stdout/stderr preserved for
diagnostics, DiscoveryResult is nil.

packages.name: gibson.daemon.v1
packages.comment:
Schema evolution policy (mission-schema-canonicalization Requirement 7):

 1. Enum values (MissionStatus, etc.) are append-only. No renumbers,
 no deletions. Deprecated values use `[deprecated = true]` plus a
 `// reserved` comment.
 2. Message field numbers are append-only. No renumbers, no reuse.
 Type-of-field changes ARE breaking and require a ship sequence
 across SDK + every consumer (see ADR 0004 for the precedent).
 3. Cross-file consistency: this file consumes
 gibson.mission.v1.MissionDefinition AND
 gibson.mission.v1.MissionConstraints (the canonical platform-wide
 constraint shape per ADR 0004). The daemon-local MissionConstraints
 message was removed in the same change. Any breaking change to the
 canonical SDK type must be coordinated with this file under the
 canonical ship sequence.

services.name: DaemonService
services.comment:
DaemonService provides the gRPC API for Gibson daemon client communication.

This service exposes operational daemon functionality including mission execution,
agent management, and real-time event streaming for the TUI and SDK clients.

methods.name: BuildComponent
methods.comment:
BuildComponent rebuilds a component (agent, tool, or plugin) from source.
Useful for rebuilding after manual code changes.

methods.name: CompleteMissionCUE
methods.comment:
CompleteMissionCUE returns completion candidates at a cursor position.
Powers the dashboard CUE editor's auto-complete.

methods.name: Connect
methods.comment:
Connect establishes a client connection to the daemon.
Returns connection metadata and daemon version info.

methods.name: CreateMission
methods.comment:
CreateMission creates a new mission with target and mission-definition reference.
Supports both referenced and inline configurations.

methods.name: CreateMissionDefinition
methods.comment:
CreateMissionDefinition registers a structured mission definition with the
daemon. This is the API-only replacement for the removed InstallMission RPC:
the daemon does not clone git repositories or parse YAML; callers submit a
fully-formed MissionDefinition proto (serialized from JSON in the CLI via
protojson, or constructed natively in the dashboard).

methods.name: CreateTarget
methods.comment:
CreateTarget registers a new target and returns its server-minted UUID.
The id field of the supplied target is ignored; the daemon mints it.

methods.name: DeleteTarget
methods.comment: DeleteTarget removes a target by its UUID.

methods.name: GetAgentStatus
methods.comment: GetAgentStatus returns the current status of a specific agent.

methods.name: GetCapabilityManifest
methods.comment:
GetCapabilityManifest returns the signed, versioned capability manifest
for the calling principal in their resolved tenant. SDKs call this on
session start and on invalidation events. The ADK calls it at scaffold
time to discover what components, permissions, cross-component rules,
and runtime limits apply.

methods.name: GetComponentLogs
methods.comment:
GetComponentLogs streams log entries for a component.
Supports follow mode for continuous streaming and line limits.

methods.name: GetMissionDefinition
methods.comment:
GetMissionDefinition returns the full structured proto for a single
installed mission definition, looked up by name. Use this instead of
ListMissionDefinitions when the caller knows the definition name and
needs every author-facing field (workspace, constraints, per-node
retry/data/reuse policies). Returns codes.NotFound when the name is
not registered.
Spec: mission-author-experience M5 (gibson#134).

methods.name: GetMissionGraph
methods.comment:
GetMissionGraph returns the renderable flow-chart projection of a mission
definition: typed nodes (boxes), data-flow edges, derived entry/exit, and
per-node positions. The daemon computes the topology and a deterministic
auto-layout from the mission DAG, then overlays any saved layout from the
mission layout store (SaveMissionLayout) so hand-arranged positions win.
This keeps the dashboard a pure renderer — it never re-derives topology.
Presentation only: nothing here affects mission execution.
Spec: MissionGraph epic (sdk#278).

methods.name: GetMissionHistory
methods.comment:
GetMissionHistory returns all runs for a mission name, showing the
complete history of mission executions with the same mission name.

methods.name: GetMissionLayout
methods.comment:
GetMissionLayout returns the saved diagram layout (per-node positions +
viewport) for a mission definition, or an empty layout when none has been
saved. The layout store is separate from the mission definition record —
the mission work-schema carries no presentation state. Keyed by
mission_definition_id. Spec: MissionGraph epic (sdk#278).

methods.name: GetMyPermissions
methods.comment:
GetMyPermissions returns the current user's role, is_admin flag, component
grants, and team memberships for the current tenant. Used by the
dashboard's PermissionsCache to gate UI elements without per-click daemon
calls.

Auth: self-mode (spec: self-mode-authz). The hotfix `unauthenticated: true`
is replaced with `self: true + allowed_identities: USER`. This RPC may be
called before the active-tenant cookie is set (which made the earlier
`tenant_from_identity` permissions check fail with "no tenant derivable"), so no
permissions tuple lookup is performed. The four defense layers are preserved:
 (a) `` validates the the identity service JWT before the authorization layer.
 (b) the authorization layer mints X-Gibson-Identity-Subject from the verified sub —
 clients cannot forge it.
 (c) The daemon's workload identity mTLS init is fail-closed (zero-trust-hardening
 Req 1) so non- callers cannot reach the listener.
 (d) the authorization layer enforces allowed_identities: only USER tokens are accepted.
The handler scopes the response strictly to the caller's verified subject.

methods.name: GetTarget
methods.comment: GetTarget returns a single target by its UUID.

methods.name: HoverMissionCUE
methods.comment:
HoverMissionCUE returns type and documentation for a position in CUE source.
Powers the dashboard CUE editor's hover tooltip.

methods.name: ListAgents
methods.comment: ListAgents returns all registered agents from the etcd registry.

methods.name: ListMissionDefinitions
methods.comment: ListMissionDefinitions returns all installed mission definitions.

methods.name: ListMissions
methods.comment: ListMissions returns all missions (past and active).

methods.name: ListMyMemberships
methods.comment:
ListMyMemberships returns every tenant the authenticated caller is a
member of, with the caller's role per tenant. Identity comes from the
call context; no tenant_id parameter — this RPC discovers the caller's
tenants. Used by the dashboard at sign-in time to populate the tenant
picker / set the active-tenant cookie.

Auth: self-mode (spec: self-mode-authz). The hotfix `unauthenticated: true`
is replaced with `self: true + allowed_identities: USER`. By definition this
RPC runs before the caller's active tenant is known, so a
`tenant_from_identity` deriver would always fail "no tenant derivable". The
same four defense layers as GetMyPermissions apply; see that method for the
full contract. The handler self-scopes the membership list to the verified
caller subject.

methods.name: ListPlugins
methods.comment: ListPlugins returns all registered plugins from the etcd registry.

methods.name: ListTargets
methods.comment: ListTargets returns the calling tenant's targets, narrowed by TargetFilter.

methods.name: ListTools
methods.comment: ListTools returns all registered tools from the etcd registry.

methods.name: PauseMission
methods.comment:
PauseMission pauses a running mission at the next clean checkpoint boundary.
If force is true, pauses immediately without waiting for a clean boundary.

methods.name: Ping
methods.comment:
Ping checks if the daemon is responsive.
Used for health checks and connection validation.

methods.name: QueryPlugin
methods.comment:
QueryPlugin executes a method on a plugin and returns the result.
The plugin must be registered in the etcd registry.

methods.name: RenewCapabilityGrant
methods.comment:
RenewCapabilityGrant mints a fresh capability-grant JWT for an
ongoing mission task whose existing CG-JWT is approaching its
≤30-minute expiry. Long-running missions (vuln research, broad
recon sweeps, multi-host fuzzing) call this before their current
CG-JWT expires so callbacks keep flowing without dispatching a
fresh task.

Authorization: the caller MUST present a valid (non-expired)
CG-JWT whose subject matches the request's agent_id and whose
mission_id/task_id match the request. Renewal is rate-limited
per agent to prevent abuse.

Spec: unified-identity-and-authorization Requirement 5.8.

methods.name: ResumeMission
methods.comment:
ResumeMission resumes a paused mission from its last checkpoint.
Returns a stream of mission events as execution continues.

methods.name: RunMission
methods.comment:
RunMission starts a mission and streams execution events.
The stream remains open until the mission completes or is stopped.

methods.name: SaveMissionLayout
methods.comment:
SaveMissionLayout persists a hand-arranged diagram layout for a mission
definition into the layout store. Layout-only: it never mutates the mission
definition, its nodes/edges/configs, or its cue_source. The optional
expected_version enables optimistic concurrency — a stale write (the layout
changed underneath) is rejected rather than clobbering. Keyed by
mission_definition_id. Spec: MissionGraph epic (sdk#278).

methods.name: ShowComponent
methods.comment:
ShowComponent returns detailed information about a component.

methods.name: StartComponent

StartComponent starts a component (agent, tool, or plugin) by kind and name.
The component must be installed in the local database.

service endpoints, and component counts.

If force is true, sends SIGKILL immediately instead of graceful SIGTERM.

methods.name: StopMission

methods.name: Subscribe
methods.comment:
Subscribe establishes an event stream for TUI real-time updates.
Streams mission events, agent events, finding events, etc.

methods.name: UpdateMissionDefinition
methods.comment:
UpdateMissionDefinition replaces the content of an existing mission
definition. The name field of the embedded definition is the lookup key.
All other fields replace the stored definition; the server-assigned ID and
original timestamps are preserved. Returns codes.NotFound if no definition
with that name exists.
Spec: gibson#437.

methods.name: ValidateMissionCUE

ValidateMissionCUE compiles a CUE mission snippet and returns diagnostics.
Powers the dashboard CUE editor's real-time error squiggles, and is now
callable by ADK/SDK users with a single user token. An empty diagnostics
list means the source is valid.

methods.name: WatchManifestInvalidations
methods.comment:
WatchManifestInvalidations streams ManifestInvalidationEvents to the
caller whenever their resolved tenant's manifest is invalidated (permissions
mutation, component registry change, tier update). Heartbeats are
emitted periodically to keep the stream alive.

messages.comment:

fields.comment: name is the mission name

fields.name: constraints
fields.comment:
constraints defines dispatch-time execution constraints. Canonical type
per ADR 0004: gibson.mission.v1.MissionConstraints is the single
platform-wide shape.

Precedence: dispatch-time constraints (this field) take full precedence
over any constraints baked into the referenced MissionDefinition. There
is NO per-field merge — if this field is set, the entire dispatch
constraint set wins; any field absent from this message reverts to 0
(unlimited), not to the definition's value.

To inherit the definition's constraints, leave this field unset (the
zero-value message is NOT the same as "absent"). Callers that want
partial overrides must read the definition's constraints first and
re-supply all fields they wish to preserve.

Token budget precedence for per-call caps:
 dispatch constraints.max_tokens_per_call
 > definition constraints.max_tokens_per_call
 > per-node *NodeConfig.max_tokens_per_call (lowest; wins if set)

Spec: ADR 0004, mission-schema-canonicalization; gibson#133 (M4).

mission. Optional. When non-empty, the daemon stores it alongside the
structured mission state. Empty for programmatic callers that never had
a YAML source.

services.name: GraphService
services.comment:
GraphService serves per-tenant knowledge-graph reads and a server-streaming
update feed. Every RPC routes through Pool.For(tenant).the knowledge graph server-side
and is gated by the permissions tenant.member relation at the authorization layer.

methods.name: GetFindingCounts
methods.comment:
GetFindingCounts returns finding counts grouped by severity or category.
Replaces the dashboard's prior direct-the knowledge graph paths in
the dashboard data client (getKPIs, getFindingsBySeverity, getFindingsByCategory)
and app/api/findings/counts/route.ts.

methods.name: GetFindingTimeSeries
methods.comment:
GetFindingTimeSeries returns finding counts bucketed by day for the last
N days (default 30, max 365). Missing days are returned as zero buckets.

methods.name: GetFindings
methods.comment:
GetFindings returns a paginated, filterable list of findings (and
vulnerabilities) for the calling tenant. Replaces the dashboard's
direct-the knowledge graph paths in app/api/findings/route.ts,
app/api/missions/[id]/findings/route.ts, and the iteration backing
findings export.
Spec: dashboard-the knowledge graph-crud-removal Req 1.

methods.name: GetGraphContext
methods.comment:
GetGraphContext returns a focus node and its bounded neighborhood, used
by the chatbot to enrich its system prompt. Returns an empty response
(focus_node unset) on missing node or NotProvisioned — does NOT error,
so the chatbot prompt never breaks.

methods.name: GetGraphStats
methods.comment:
GetGraphStats returns aggregate stats for the per-tenant knowledge graph:
node counts by label, total edges, last-write timestamp.

methods.name: GetGraphSummary
methods.comment:
GetGraphSummary returns an LLM-friendly text summary of the per-tenant
graph plus structured stats. Server-side caches results for 60s per
tenant.

methods.name: GetMissionGraph
methods.comment:
GetMissionGraph returns the subgraph touched by a single mission run.
Mission ownership is enforced by permissions + by `WHERE m.tenant_id = $tenant`
in the underlying Cypher (defense in depth).

methods.name: GetTenantGraph
methods.comment:
GetTenantGraph returns the full per-tenant subgraph subject to a server-side
node-count cap. Use limit + include_labels to narrow scope.

methods.name: QueryPaths
methods.comment:
QueryPaths runs a bounded path query from `from_node_id` to either a
specific `to_node_id` or any node of `to_node_kind`, up to `max_depth`.
Server caps: depth ≤ 10, paths ≤ 100, query timeout 5s.

methods.name: WatchGraphUpdates
methods.comment:
WatchGraphUpdates server-streams new node/edge writes for the calling

messages.name: Finding
messages.comment:
Finding is a per-tenant security finding or vulnerability node from the
knowledge graph, shaped for dashboard list/detail views.

fields.name: type
fields.comment:
Category / type. Free-form string drawn from the underlying node's
type property (e.g. "sql_injection", "exposed_secret").

fields.name: severity
fields.comment: "critical" | "high" | "medium" | "low" | "info" (lowercase, free-form).

fields.name: properties
fields.comment:
Catch-all for additional properties beyond the structured fields above
(CVE, CVSS, etc.). Values are stringified to preserve fidelity through
proto3.

fields.name: labels
fields.comment: Distinguishes:Finding from:Vulnerability and any future label split.

fields.name: time_window_seconds
fields.comment:
Optional. When > 0, only count findings whose created_at is within the
last N seconds. 0 (default) means all-time.

fields.comment: Default 30, max 365 (server-clamped).

fields.name: points
fields.comment: Ordered, padded with zero buckets for missing days. Length == days.

fields.name: category_filter
fields.comment: Exact match on the type / category. Empty string = no filter.

fields.name: mission_id
fields.comment:
When non-empty, only findings reachable from this mission node within
the same tenant (within 3 hops) are returned.

fields.name: search

Substring match on name OR description (case-insensitive). Empty = no

fields.name: limit
fields.comment: Default 100, max 500 (server-clamped).

fields.name: total
fields.comment: Count of matching findings without limit/offset, for pagination UI.

fields.name: truncated
fields.comment: True when total > offset + len(findings).

fields.name: hops
fields.comment: Default 2, max 5 (server-clamped).

fields.name: max_nodes
fields.comment: Default 30, max 100 (server-clamped).

fields.name: focus_node
fields.comment:
Unset when the node was not found OR the knowledge graph is unavailable. The daemon
returns this shape (not an error) so chatbot prompts never break.

fields.name: summary
fields.comment: LLM-friendly text serialization of focus + neighbors.

fields.name: last_write_at
fields.comment: Zero when the tenant has never written a node.

fields.name: summary
fields.comment: LLM-friendly text summary, capped at ~4000 chars.

fields.name: limit
fields.comment: Optional. Default 1000, max 5000 (server-clamped).

fields.name: include_labels

Optional. If non-empty, only nodes carrying ANY of these labels are
returned (and their connecting edges).

fields.name: truncated
fields.comment: True when total_node_count exceeded the limit and the response was capped.

Total node count for the tenant before truncation. UI should surface a
"showing N of M" banner when truncated is true.

HarnessCallbackService provides the harness interface for agents executing in standalone mode.
The SDK's CallbackHarness forwards all harness operations to the orchestrator via this service.

methods.name: Authorize
methods.comment:
Authorization Operations
Authorize checks whether the calling component's current work execution
is permitted to perform action on resource. The daemon resolves the
run_id to a (user_id, tenant_id) pair and consults permissions.

methods.comment: Tool Operations

Mission Management Operations
These enable agents to autonomously create, run, and manage missions

methods.name: DevboxExec
methods.comment:
DevboxExec runs one command in the caller's session Devbox — a
session-lifetime sandbox resolved (and lazily created on first call)
by (tenant, session_id), then REUSED across calls in that session.
This is deliberately distinct from the per-call SANDBOXED tool path
(CallToolProto), which stays one microVM per call; a Devbox holds
working state (checkouts, build caches) that per-call isolation would
throw away between commands.

methods.name: Observe
methods.comment:
Observe emits a typed observation into the World (ADR-0007). The brain
resolves identity and topology; scope is derived server-side from context.

methods.name: PutSessionContext
methods.comment:
Session-context store: an opaque, versioned blob per (tenant,
session_id), persisted in the per-tenant dataplane store. The daemon
never interprets the bytes — the component owns its own format. This
is the TRUSTED home for a session's local context; it must never be
written to the untrusted Devbox volume (that invariant is the
client's to keep, but this store is why keeping it costs nothing).
Writes are guarded by an etag (If-Match) so concurrent writers cannot
clobber each other; the server enforces a TTL and a size cap.

methods.comment:
SearchTools returns a small, ranked, authz-filtered set of tools matching
a query — the meta-tool surface agents use instead of receiving every tool
(ADR-0047 facet 5). Per-tool authorization is enforced inside the handler;
this RPC-level gate only checks that the caller may use the harness.

methods.name: WorkspaceCommit
methods.comment:
WorkspaceCommit stages all changes in the workspace and creates a
commit with the given message. Returns the commit SHA.

methods.name: WorkspaceGetInfo
methods.comment:
WorkspaceGetInfo returns name + path for a single workspace. An empty
name resolves to the mission's primary workspace (single-repo case).
Returns NOT_FOUND when no workspace with that name exists.

methods.name: WorkspaceList
methods.comment:
WorkspaceList returns metadata for every workspace configured for
the calling component's active mission. Returns an empty list when
the mission has no workspaces.

methods.name: WorkspaceListFiles
methods.comment:
WorkspaceListFiles returns paths matching the given glob pattern,
relative to the workspace root. Result sets larger than 10,000 paths
are truncated to the first 10,000 with truncated=true on the
response.

methods.name: WorkspacePush
methods.comment:
WorkspacePush pushes committed changes to the remote configured for
the workspace. Returns PERMISSION_DENIED on auth failure against
the remote.

methods.name: WorkspaceReadFile
methods.comment:
WorkspaceReadFile reads a file from the named workspace. Path is
relative to the workspace root. Files larger than 16 MB return
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; a streaming variant is deferred to a follow-on
spec.

methods.name: WorkspaceWriteFile
methods.comment:
WorkspaceWriteFile writes content to a file in the named workspace.
Path is relative to the workspace root. Content larger than 16 MB
returns RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; a streaming variant is deferred.

methods.name: WorldView
methods.comment:
WorldView returns the caller's server-projected slice of the tenant World
(ADR-0012, sdk#341's read half). It is the counterpart to Observe: Observe
is the agent's only write, WorldView its only read.

The slice is projected by the daemon from the mission record it created —
the tenant that owns the World and the scope that bounds the slice are read
there, never from this request. WorldViewRequest carries no tenant field and
no scope field, so an agent cannot name another tenant's World or a wider
slice: both are unrepresentable rather than rejected.

messages.name: AuthorizeRequest

It does not expose internal permissions object names or user IDs.

messages.comment: WorkspaceGetInfoRequest fetches metadata for a single workspace.

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
Empty name resolves to the mission's primary workspace
(single-repository missions).

messages.name: WorkspaceGetInfoResponse
messages.comment: WorkspaceGetInfoResponse carries the requested workspace metadata.

fields.name: workspace
fields.comment: Absent on NOT_FOUND.

messages.name: WorkspaceInfo
messages.comment: WorkspaceInfo is the minimal name + path projection of a workspace.

fields.name: name
fields.comment: name is the repository identifier from the mission's WorkspaceConfig.

fields.name: path
fields.comment:
path is the absolute path to the workspace root on the daemon. Useful
for log attribution; the callback agent does not access this path.

messages.name: WorkspaceListFilesRequest
messages.comment: WorkspaceListFilesRequest enumerates workspace files matching a glob.

fields.name: workspace_name
fields.comment: Empty workspace_name resolves to the primary workspace.

fields.name: pattern
fields.comment:
pattern is a glob matched relative to the workspace root.
Examples: "*.go", "**/*.py", "src/**/*.ts".

messages.name: WorkspaceListFilesResponse
messages.comment:
WorkspaceListFilesResponse carries the matched paths, with a truncation
flag when the result set exceeded the 10,000-path cap.

fields.name: truncated
fields.comment:
truncated is true when the result was capped at 10,000 paths and more
matches exist. Refine the pattern to drill in.

messages.name: WorkspaceListRequest
messages.comment:
WorkspaceListRequest enumerates workspaces for the calling mission.
The mission scope is derived from the request context (set by the SDK
CallbackClient via contextInfo — same pattern as the memory RPCs).

messages.name: WorkspaceListResponse
messages.comment: WorkspaceListResponse carries every workspace in the mission.

messages.name: WorkspacePushRequest
messages.comment: WorkspacePushRequest pushes committed changes to the workspace's remote.

fields.name: workspace_name
fields.comment: Empty workspace_name resolves to the primary workspace.

messages.name: WorkspacePushResponse
messages.comment: WorkspacePushResponse is empty on success.

messages.name: WorkspaceReadFileRequest
messages.comment: WorkspaceReadFileRequest reads a file from a workspace.

fields.name: workspace_name
fields.comment: Empty workspace_name resolves to the primary workspace.

fields.name: path
fields.comment: Path is relative to the workspace root.

messages.name: WorkspaceReadFileResponse
messages.comment: WorkspaceReadFileResponse carries the file's full content.

messages.name: WorkspaceWriteFileRequest
messages.comment: WorkspaceWriteFileRequest writes content to a file in a workspace.

fields.name: workspace_name
fields.comment: Empty workspace_name resolves to the primary workspace.

fields.name: path
fields.comment: Path is relative to the workspace root.

fields.name: content
fields.comment: Content is the new file body. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED if > 16 MB.

messages.name: WorkspaceWriteFileResponse
messages.comment: WorkspaceWriteFileResponse is empty on success.

messages.name: WorldEntity
messages.comment: WorldEntity is one entity in the slice.

fields.name: handle
fields.comment:
handle is the ONLY name the agent has for this entity: an opaque,
server-minted, non-constructible reference, valid within the slice it was
issued to and nowhere else. It carries no brain id an agent could iterate,
so enumerating past the slice boundary is unrepresentable (ADR-0012).

A handle stays stable across re-projections of the same slice: the entity
it names does not change, so refreshing the view never invalidates a
reference the agent is holding.

fields.name: label
fields.comment:
label is the entity's coordinate as observed — an address, an FQDN, a
finding title. Human- and LLM-readable; not a reference (only handle is).

fields.name: attributes
fields.comment:
attributes is the projected detail, level-of-detail summarized for the
unfocused slice and complete for a focused one. Keys are server-chosen.

messages.name: WorldViewRequest
messages.comment:
WorldViewRequest asks for the caller's slice of the tenant World.

There is deliberately no tenant field and no scope field. The daemon reads both
off the mission record it created, reached through the harness registered for
(mission_id, agent_name); context is an address that selects which harness to
consult, never an authority over what the slice contains. An agent therefore
cannot express "another tenant's World" or "a wider scope" at all.

fields.name: focus
fields.comment:
focus narrows the response to entities the caller was already shown, by
their handles, and returns those at full detail instead of the summary
level the unfocused slice carries. A handle that was not issued to this
caller is refused — focus can never widen a slice, only zoom into one.

messages.name: WorldViewResponse
messages.comment: WorldViewResponse carries the projected slice.

fields.name: truncated
fields.comment:
truncated is true when the slice exceeded the projection cap and entities
were dropped. The cap is a server-side budget, not something the caller can
raise; a truncated slice is still a valid one.

enums.name: CredentialType
enums.comment: CredentialType represents the type of credential.

enums.name: MemoryTier
enums.comment: MemoryTier specifies which memory tier to use for an operation.

enums.name: MissionStatus
enums.comment: MissionStatus represents the current state of a mission.

enums.name: SpanKind
enums.comment: SpanKind represents the role of a span in a distributed trace.

enums.name: StatusCode
enums.comment: StatusCode represents the status of a span.

enums.name: WorldEntityKind
enums.comment: WorldEntityKind names what an entity in the slice is.

packages.name: gibson.identity.v1
packages.comment:
Package gibson.identity.v1 — caller-side identity inspection.

IdentityService.WhoAmI is the canonical "what can I do?" RPC. Every
authenticated principal may call it for themselves; tenant_admins
may pass target_principal_id to inspect another agent in their
tenant. The response carries the caller's effective permissions grants
(component reads/writes/executes, plugin invocations) and any
active capability grants.

Spec: component-bootstrap-e2e Requirement 10.

methods.name: WhoAmI
methods.comment:
WhoAmI returns the caller's effective permissions grants. When
target_principal_id is set, the caller MUST be tenant_admin on
the target's tenant — otherwise the daemon returns
PermissionDenied. Identity is derived from the authorization layer-emitted
headers, never from the request body.

messages.name: ComponentGrantEffective
messages.comment:
ComponentGrantEffective describes the principal's per-action access
to one component (permissions type "component"). The three booleans reflect
the per-action permissions relations as composed by model.fga's deny-wins
rules: each is true iff the principal can perform that action right
now after all denies are subtracted.

fields.name: component_ref
fields.comment: component_ref is the permissions object identifier, e.g. "component:gitlab".

fields.name: sources
fields.comment:
sources enumerates how the principal got each granted action.
For UI legibility — multiple sources may stack (direct grant
plus tenant-member inheritance, etc.).

messages.name: GrantSource
messages.comment:
GrantSource attributes a single grant to its origin in the permissions model.
Used by the dashboard's Permissions tab to render inheritance and by
gibson inspect to show the operator where a permission came from.

fields.name: source_object
fields.comment:
source_object is the permissions object the inheritance flowed from
(e.g. "tenant:zeroroot-ai", "team:red"). Empty for KIND_DIRECT.

messages.name: PluginGrantEffective
messages.comment:
PluginGrantEffective describes the principal's invocation access to
one plugin (permissions type "plugin", binary can_invoke).

messages.name: WhoAmIRequest
messages.comment:
WhoAmIRequest carries an optional target_principal_id for admin
inspection. When empty, the caller's own identity (from the authorization layer
headers) is used.

fields.name: target_principal_id
fields.comment:
target_principal_id is OPTIONAL. When set, the caller MUST be
tenant_admin on the target's tenant. Format matches the permissions
user form: "agent_principal:<uuid>" / "tool_principal:<uuid>" /
"plugin_principal:<uuid>".

messages.name: WhoAmIResponse
messages.comment: WhoAmIResponse carries the principal's effective grants.

fields.name: principal_id
fields.comment:
principal_id is the permissions principal identifier of the principal
this response describes.

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
name is the human-readable name the principal was registered with
(e.g. "scanner-bot"). Used for display; not used for authz.

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.comment: tenant_id is the tenant the principal belongs to.

fields.name: component_grants
fields.comment:
component_grants is one entry per component the principal can
touch in any way (read, configure, or execute). Components the
principal cannot touch are NOT included.

fields.name: plugin_grants
fields.comment:
plugin_grants is one entry per plugin the principal can invoke.
For agent_principals this is empty by permissions model design (agents
do not directly invoke plugins; tools do).

fields.name: active_capability_grants
fields.comment:
active_capability_grants is the principal's currently-issued
CG-JWTs (mission-scoped) at the time of the call. Reuses the
public CapabilityGrantInfo message from gibson.capability.v1
(extracted from gibson.admin.v1 in slice #108) rather than
minting a parallel type.

fields.name: truncated
fields.comment:
truncated is true when the response had to drop entries to fit
within the 1000-grant safety bound documented in
component-bootstrap-e2e Requirement 10.4. Callers seeing this
flag should treat the listing as incomplete and surface a UI
warning.

fields.name: can_revoke_sessions
fields.comment:
can_revoke_sessions is a COARSE capability flag: true when the
principal holds a tenant/team admin role that lets it revoke the
sessions of at least some members (composed from self +
tenant#admin-over-member + team#admin-over-member; see
RevokeUserSessions / gibson#622). It exists so admin UIs
(dashboard#717) can gate "revoke sessions" button visibility
without a trial-and-error RPC.

It is deliberately NOT per-target: the authoritative,
per-(caller,target) decision is still made inside
RevokeUserSessions, which fails closed for targets the caller may
not revoke. A false value means "show no revoke UI"; a true value
means "this principal can revoke someone — let the RPC enforce who."

values.name: KIND_DIRECT
values.comment: KIND_DIRECT — tuple writes the principal directly.

values.name: KIND_TENANT_MEMBER
values.comment: KIND_TENANT_MEMBER — inherited via tenant#member.

values.name: KIND_TEAM_MEMBER
values.comment: KIND_TEAM_MEMBER — inherited via team#member.

values.name: KIND_OWNER
values.comment:
KIND_OWNER — granted because the principal's tenant owns the
component (admin-from-owner permissions path).

enums.name: PrincipalKind
enums.comment:
PrincipalKind identifies the runtime kind of a Gibson principal.

Canonical home: this enum is the SDK-published source of truth. The
daemon's local tenant_admin proto and the SDK's RecipientClass enum
in gibson.admin.v1.grants are duplicates that pre-date the
component-bootstrap-e2e consolidation; both should migrate to
importing PrincipalKind from this package over time.

messages.name: AgentContract
messages.comment:
AgentContract describes an agent's LLM slot surface and declared
tool/plugin dependencies. The daemon composes this from the agent's
descriptor RPC at registration time.

messages.name: CapabilityManifest
messages.comment:
CapabilityManifest is the single, signed, versioned snapshot of every
component, permission, cross-component rule, and runtime context that
applies to the calling principal in their resolved tenant. Both SDKs
(runtime) and the ADK (scaffold-time) consume this shape.

fields.name: signature
fields.comment: Signature payload (Ed25519 over body with signature/kid cleared).

messages.name: ComponentCapability
messages.comment:
ComponentCapability is a single discoverable component (agent, tool, plugin)
enriched with the permissions the subject holds against it, plus a typed
contract describing how to invoke it.

Kind discriminator (component-bootstrap-e2e R12): the typed
`principal_kind` field is the canonical way to branch on
agent/tool/plugin. The legacy `string kind = 2` is retained for
backward compatibility during the one-minor-release deprecation
window — readers SHOULD prefer `principal_kind` and SHOULD validate
that the populated `contract` oneof matches the kind.

fields.name: kind
fields.comment:
DEPRECATED: prefer `principal_kind`. String-form kind for legacy
consumers; one-minor-release deprecation window.

fields.name: principal_kind
fields.comment:
principal_kind is the typed kind discriminator. Populated by the
daemon at manifest-resolution time; set by the SDK loader when
converting YAML manifests. Must agree with the populated
`contract` oneof (PRINCIPAL_KIND_AGENT ↔ agent_contract, etc.) —
mismatches are rejected by the daemon's RegisterPlugin /
CreateAgentIdentity validators.

Spec: component-bootstrap-e2e Requirement 12.

messages.name: ComponentLiveness
messages.comment:
ComponentLiveness is a snapshot of the component's runtime health at
manifest issuance time. It is advisory only; the daemon remains the
source of truth for live execution decisions.

messages.name: CrossComponentRule
messages.comment:
CrossComponentRule expresses an explicit override on the default
can_execute evaluation for a (source_component, target_component) pair.
Only rules that override the default are emitted, keeping payload bounded.

messages.name: GetCapabilityManifestRequest
messages.comment:
GetCapabilityManifestRequest identifies the subject whose manifest is
requested. agent_principal_id is only honored for tenant admins and
enables scaffold-time impersonation previews.

messages.name: GetCapabilityManifestResponse
messages.comment:
GetCapabilityManifestResponse wraps the signed manifest. Wrapping keeps
the RPC Buf-STANDARD compliant and leaves room for envelope metadata
(e.g. server-side issuance metrics) to be added without breaking the
wire format of the manifest body itself.

messages.name: LimitsAndQuotas
messages.comment:
LimitsAndQuotas carries the tier-derived resource ceilings applied to
the subject's session. max_spend_usd is a decimal string to avoid
floating-point rounding at quota boundaries.

messages.name: ManifestInvalidationEvent
messages.comment:
ManifestInvalidationEvent is delivered when the subject's manifest
should be considered stale. HEARTBEAT events indicate the stream is
alive; INVALIDATED events indicate a refresh is warranted.

messages.name: MemoryPermissions
messages.comment: MemoryPermissions expresses per-tier memory access (e.g. "ro", "rw", "").

messages.name: PluginContract
messages.comment:
PluginContract enumerates a plugin's callable methods with per-method
schemas and per-method permissions-derived invocation permission.

messages.name: TenantContext
messages.comment:
TenantContext surfaces the tenant identity and team memberships that
gate the manifest's scope.

messages.name: ToolContract
messages.comment:
ToolContract describes the proto envelope a tool accepts and emits.
input_schema_json and output_schema_json are derived from the
FileDescriptor and rendered to JSON Schema for SDK/ADK consumption.

fields.name: idempotency
fields.comment: see ToolIdempotency enum; UNSPECIFIED is treated as AT_LEAST_ONCE

messages.name: WatchManifestInvalidationsRequest
messages.comment:
WatchManifestInvalidationsRequest opens a server-streaming channel
emitting ManifestInvalidationEvent for the caller's resolved tenant.

messages.name: WatchManifestInvalidationsResponse
messages.comment:
WatchManifestInvalidationsResponse wraps a single invalidation event
so the RPC's streaming response type satisfies Buf STANDARD naming.

enums.name: ToolIdempotency
enums.comment:
ToolIdempotency declares the at-most-once / at-least-once / exactly-once
delivery semantics a tool guarantees. Read by the resume-from-checkpoint
logic: tools at AT_LEAST_ONCE are safely retried on resume; tools at
AT_MOST_ONCE are skipped if their pre-checkpoint invocation status is
ambiguous; tools at EXACTLY_ONCE require the orchestrator to consult the
idempotency journal before re-issuing. UNSPECIFIED is treated as
AT_LEAST_ONCE for backward compatibility.

Spec: mission-checkpointing R6.

packages.name: gibson.mission.v1
packages.comment:
Schema evolution policy (mission-schema-canonicalization Requirement 7):

 1. NodeType, Language, BackoffStrategy, and any future enum values
 are append-only. Existing values are NEVER renumbered or removed.
 2. Deprecated values are marked `[deprecated = true]` and accompanied
 by a `// reserved` comment explaining the supersession.
 3. MissionNode.config oneof variants are append-only with the same
 discipline; reuse of a tag number is forbidden.
 4. Adding a new node type or expression language requires the
 controlled-extension contract defined in
 `mission-verb-noun-registry`: a matching *NodeConfig message in
 the oneof, a registered handler in the daemon, and a conformance
 test exercising the new type end-to-end. CI enforces all four.

The proto under this package is the single source of truth for the
mission schema. The daemon, the `gibson` CLI (ADK), and the
dashboard all consume the generated bindings of this file.
Hand-written parallel representations are forbidden.

messages.name: AgentNodeConfig
messages.comment:
AgentNodeConfig contains configuration for agent nodes.
AGENT = LLM-driven worker that calls tools and plugins on the
author's behalf. The executor selects an agent component by name
and dispatches the configured Task.

fields.name: agent_name
fields.comment: AgentName is the name of the agent to execute

fields.name: task
fields.comment: Task is the agent task configuration

fields.name: max_tokens_per_call
fields.comment:
max_tokens_per_call is the per-node override of
MissionConstraints.max_tokens_per_call for this agent node only.

When present (non-nil), this value is used as the effective cap for
all LLM calls made by this node, regardless of the mission-level
MissionConstraints.max_tokens_per_call value. Setting this to 0
explicitly disables the cap for this node (the mission-level cap is
NOT applied as a fallback when this field is explicitly set to 0).

When absent (nil / proto3 optional not set), the mission-level
MissionConstraints.max_tokens_per_call applies instead.

0 = inherit from mission-level (when this field is absent).
Spec: mission-schema-canonicalization Requirement 5; gibson#133.

fields.name: llm_slots
fields.comment:
llm_slots pins LLM provider/model bindings per named slot for this agent
node. Each entry maps a slot name to a specific provider+model. Multiple
entries allow different slots to use different providers/models on the same
node. Empty list → the node inherits the tenant's default provider for all
slots. Absent slot entries fall through to tenant default + constraint
search over the tenant's permitted providers.

Empty provider or model within an entry is a valid fall-through marker:
the daemon resolves it against the tenant's configured defaults.

Precedence at resolution per slot: explicit binding in llm_slots >
tenant default > constraint search over the tenant's permitted providers.

Spec: sdk#260 (multi-slot LLM binding contract); consumer: gibson#524.

messages.name: ConditionNodeConfig
messages.comment: ConditionNodeConfig contains configuration for condition nodes

fields.name: expression
fields.comment: Expression to evaluate (e.g., "result.status == 'success'")

fields.name: true_branch
fields.comment: TrueBranch contains node IDs to execute if condition is true

fields.name: false_branch
fields.comment: FalseBranch contains node IDs to execute if condition is false

fields.name: language
fields.comment:
Language declares the expression language. Defaults to
LANGUAGE_CEL; LANGUAGE_UNSPECIFIED is treated as CEL for
backwards compatibility with pre-Language-field documents.

messages.name: DataPolicy
messages.comment:
DataPolicy defines how data is handled for a node.

Deprecated: superseded by the ECS brain (gibson#851, ADR-0008). Data
handling (reuse + scoping) is now implicit in the event-sourced World and
scope-relative identity (ADR-0002) + ambient projection. Retained
wire-compatibly; ignored by the engine.

fields.name: store_input
fields.comment: StoreInput determines whether to store input data in GraphRAG

fields.name: store_output
fields.comment: StoreOutput determines whether to store output data in GraphRAG

fields.name: retention
fields.comment: Retention specifies how long to retain data (0 = forever)

fields.name: encryption
fields.comment: Encryption determines whether data should be encrypted at rest

fields.name: access_control
fields.comment: AccessControl specifies who can access this data

messages.name: JoinNodeConfig
messages.comment:
JoinNodeConfig blocks until every node ID in `wait_for` has
completed (success or final failure), then merges their results
per `strategy`. JOIN is a first-class noun separable from
PARALLEL — a JOIN can merge results from non-parallel branches.

Spec: mission-verb-noun-registry Requirement 7.

fields.name: wait_for
strategy
fields.comment: strategy selects how upstream results are combined.

fields.name: aggregator
fields.comment:
aggregator carries a CEL expression used when strategy is
MERGE_STRATEGY_CUSTOM. The expression sees `sources` (a map
from node ID to that node's result) and returns the merged
value. Empty when strategy is not CUSTOM.

messages.name: LLMSlotConfig
messages.comment:
LLMSlotConfig pins the provider/model for an agent node's LLM slot. It is a
tenant-scoped reference: the provider name must be one the tenant has
configured (gibson.tenant provider config); model is the provider's model id
(empty = the provider's default model). Leave the whole message unset to
inherit the tenant default.

fields.name: slot
fields.comment: slot is the slot name this binding targets. Empty defaults to "primary".

fields.name: provider
fields.comment: provider is the configured provider's name for the calling tenant.

fields.name: model
fields.comment: model is the model id; empty uses the provider's default model.

messages.name: MissionConstraints
messages.comment:
MissionConstraints declares the operational limits baked into a mission
definition. Making constraints part of the schema lets mission authors
publish self-describing missions (e.g., "stop after 50 findings") without
requiring callers to supply limits out-of-band at dispatch time.

Semantics (zero means unlimited):
 - max_duration: 0 duration → no time limit
 - max_tokens: 0 → no token budget
 - max_cost: 0.0 → no cost ceiling
 - max_findings: 0 → no finding count limit

Spec: sdk#47 (MissionConstraints proto promotion).

fields.name: max_duration
fields.comment:
max_duration is the wall-clock limit for the entire mission.
Uses google.protobuf.Duration for sub-second precision.
Absent or zero-value means no time limit.

fields.name: max_tokens
fields.comment:
max_tokens is the cumulative LLM token budget across the entire mission
(all agent nodes combined). The daemon accumulates usage on every LLM
invocation and stops the mission when the budget is exceeded.
0 means unlimited. This is a mission-wide budget, not a per-call limit;
use max_tokens_per_call to cap individual invocations.

fields.name: max_cost
fields.comment:
max_cost is the cumulative LLM cost ceiling in USD across all agent
nodes. 0.0 means unlimited.

fields.name: max_findings
fields.comment:
max_findings is the maximum number of findings to collect before the
mission stops. 0 means unlimited.

fields.name: severity_threshold
fields.comment:
severity_threshold is the minimum severity level required to record a
finding. Common values: "low", "medium", "high", "critical".
Empty string means accept all severities.

fields.name: require_evidence
fields.comment:
require_evidence indicates whether all findings must include
proof-of-concept evidence before being recorded.

fields.name: blocked_tools
fields.comment:
blocked_tools lists tool names that must not be invoked during this
mission. The daemon enforces this at dispatch time.

fields.name: blocked_domains
fields.comment:
blocked_domains lists network domains (e.g., "prod.example.com") that
agents must not contact. Enforcement is best-effort at the tool level.

fields.name: max_turns_per_agent
fields.comment:
max_turns_per_agent caps the number of agent turns (Observe→Think→Act
iterations) for any single agent node in the mission. 0 means unlimited.

fields.name: allowed_techniques
fields.comment:
allowed_techniques is the allowlist of attack technique IDs (taxonomy)
that agents may use during the mission. Empty list means no allowlist
(any technique may be used unless blocked).

fields.name: blocked_techniques
fields.comment:
blocked_techniques is the blocklist of attack technique IDs that
agents must not use, regardless of allowed_techniques. Empty list
means no blocklist.

fields.name: max_tokens_per_call
fields.comment:
max_tokens_per_call is the per-invocation cap on LLM tokens for any
single LLM call within this mission. Applied by the daemon before every
provider call; the provider never sees more than this many output tokens.

Precedence cascade (highest → lowest):
 1. Per-node *NodeConfig.max_tokens_per_call (when set on a specific node)
 2. This field (mission-level default)
 3. 0 — no cap from this mechanism

When a per-node override is set it completely supersedes this field for
that node (including 0, which explicitly disables the cap for that node
while this field may still apply to all other nodes).

This field is different from max_tokens: max_tokens is a cumulative
budget for the entire mission; max_tokens_per_call is a ceiling on each
individual LLM call.

0 means unlimited at this level. Spec: mission-schema-canonicalization
Requirement 5. Enforced by EffectivePerCallCap (wired in M4, gibson#133).

messages.name: MissionDefinition
messages.comment:
MissionDefinition represents a mission template/definition.
This is the shareable mission specification that can be created via the
CreateMissionDefinition API and referenced by mission runs.

fields.name: id
fields.comment: ID is the unique identifier for this mission definition

fields.name: name
fields.comment: Name is a human-readable name for the mission

fields.name: description
fields.comment: Description provides additional context about what this mission does

fields.name: version
fields.comment: Version is the semantic version of the mission definition

fields.name: target_ref
fields.comment:
TargetRef is a reference to the target (name or ID)
This needs to be resolved to a TargetID when creating a mission instance

fields.name: nodes
fields.comment: Nodes contains all the nodes in the mission, indexed by node ID

fields.name: edges
fields.comment: Edges contains all the directed edges connecting nodes in the mission

fields.name: entry_points
fields.comment:
EntryPoints contains the IDs of nodes that can serve as entry points to the mission
These are nodes with no incoming edges

fields.name: exit_points
fields.comment:
ExitPoints contains the IDs of nodes that can serve as exit points from the mission
These are nodes with no outgoing edges

fields.name: metadata
fields.comment: Metadata contains additional custom metadata for the mission

fields.name: dependencies
fields.comment: Dependencies specifies required agents and tools for this mission

fields.name: source
fields.comment: Source is the git URL this mission was installed from (if applicable)

fields.name: installed_at
fields.comment: InstalledAt is the timestamp when this mission was installed

fields.name: created_at
fields.comment: CreatedAt is the timestamp when the mission definition was created

fields.name: workspace
fields.comment:
Workspace configures repository cloning + workspace
management for agents that need code access. Optional;
missions without code interaction omit this field.

Spec: mission-schema-canonicalization (mirror migration).

fields.name: constraints
fields.comment:
Constraints declares mission-level operational limits. When present,
these are the authoritative constraints for the mission DAG — they
make the mission self-describing so authors do not have to supply limits
out-of-band at dispatch time. The daemon merges these with any
dispatch-time overrides (dispatch wins on conflict).
Optional: absent means no constraints are baked into the definition.

Spec: sdk#47 (MissionConstraints proto promotion).

fields.name: decider_slot
fields.comment:
DeciderSlot names the mission-level LLM the brain's Decider runs on — the
orchestration decision-maker, distinct from per-node agent slots
(gibson#850). Only the provider+model are used (the slot name is implicitly
"decider"). Absent means the brain uses the tenant's dashboard-default
provider/model, so missions need not set it.

messages.name: MissionDependencies
messages.comment: MissionDependencies specifies required components for a mission

fields.name: agents
fields.comment: Agents lists required agent components by name or URL

fields.name: tools
fields.comment: Tools lists required tool components by name or URL

fields.name: plugins
fields.comment: Plugins lists required plugin components by name or URL

messages.name: MissionEdge
messages.comment: MissionEdge represents a directed edge in the mission DAG

fields.name: from
fields.comment: From is the source node ID

fields.name: to
fields.comment: To is the destination node ID

fields.name: condition
fields.comment: Condition is an optional condition that must be satisfied for the edge to be traversed

fields.name: metadata
fields.comment: Metadata contains additional metadata for the edge

messages.name: MissionNode
messages.comment: MissionNode represents a single node in a mission DAG

fields.name: id
fields.comment: ID is the unique identifier for this node within the mission

fields.name: type
fields.comment: Type is the node type

fields.name: name
fields.comment: Name is a human-readable name for the node

fields.name: description
fields.comment: Description provides additional context about this node

fields.name: agent_config
fields.comment: AgentConfig for agent nodes

ECS brain (gibson#851, ADR-0008) reuse is implicit in the event-sourced
World and scoping flows from scope-relative identity (ADR-0002) +

JoinConfig for join nodes (mission-verb-noun-registry).
